description: Exercise the generator end-to-end to produce demonstration output and prove the pipeline works. Install Argos Translate + the en->pt model, run a real (sampled) fetch+translate pass, and regenerate at least data/dictionaries/pt-br/skills.json with real GW2 skill data translated to PT-BR. Do NOT run the full ~90k items dataset; a representative sample is sufficient. This validates the API layer, translation layer, caching/resumability, and output-schema compatibility against the actual C++ loader format. Depends on FEAT-001.
steps: Create and use a virtualenv: python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate, then pip install -r tools/dictionary-generator/requirements.txt. If the full Argos install or heavy transitive deps (ctranslate2/torch) fail or time out in the sandbox, record that in findings and fall back to producing a demonstration sample using --no-translate (real EN data, structure-correct JSON) so the pipeline is still proven; do NOT mark blocked solely because model download is slow.

Install the en->pt model: python3 tools/dictionary-generator/generate_dictionaries.py --install-model (or the equivalent action). Confirm argostranslate.translate can translate a sample string EN->PT.

Run a sampled skills generation, e.g.: python3 tools/dictionary-generator/generate_dictionaries.py --category skills --limit 300 (choose a limit that completes in a reasonable time; the goal is a real, non-trivial sample, ideally the full ~few-thousand skills if time permits). Confirm the raw cache under tools/dictionary-generator/cache/ is populated and that a re-run is fast (cache hit).

Verify the produced data/dictionaries/pt-br/skills.json parses with json.load, has top-level locale=pt-br, category=skills, version=1.0.0, and a non-trivial entries array where every entry has non-empty string 'en' and 'translated'. Confirm the pre-existing curated example entries are not required (the generator output is the demonstration) and note in findings how many entries were produced.
Demonstrate resumability: interrupt-free re-run of the same command should reuse cache and not re-fetch/re-translate (verify via the summary counts / cache-hit reporting).
Record in the feature findings: which categories were run, sample sizes, whether Argos model installed successfully, runtime observed, and any fallbacks used.
acceptance_criteria: data/dictionaries/pt-br/skills.json is regenerated by the tool and contains a non-trivial number of real GW2 skill entries (substantially more than the original 15 examples), each with 'en' and 'translated' string fields.
The generated skills.json parses via json.load and matches the schema in src/translation/dictionary.cpp (locale/category/version/entries with en+translated).
The tools/dictionary-generator/cache/ directory is populated with raw EN data and (if translation ran) a translation cache, proving idempotent/resumable behavior.
A second run of the same command completes quickly using the cache (documented in findings).
If Argos could not be fully installed/run in the sandbox, findings clearly state the fallback used and confirm the pipeline is otherwise functional.
verification: Run: python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open('data/dictionaries/pt-br/skills.json')); assert d['locale']=='pt-br' and d['category']=='skills'; e=d['entries']; assert isinstance(e,list) and len(e)>15; assert all(isinstance(x['en'],str) and x['en'] and isinstance(x['translated'],str) and x['translated'] for x in e); print('OK', len(e), 'entries')"
Run: ls -la tools/dictionary-generator/cache/ and confirm raw cache (and translations.json if translation ran) exist
Re-run the sampled skills command and confirm it reports cache hits / completes quickly
